items.quote: Collecting Data
items.text: 3-1 Collecting Data

items.quote: What you'll learn
items.text: Resources of collecting data; Methods of collecting data; How to select a sample; Types of samples

items.text: The method of collecting data is considered one of the most important phases that statistical research mainly depends on. Collecting data in such scientific methods will lead to get accurate outcomes when doing operations of statistical inferrence and proper decision making.

items.quote: What are the resources of collecting data?
items.text: What are the resources of collecting data?

items.quote: How is the method of collecting data identified?
items.text: How is the method of collecting data identified?

items.quote: Resources of collecting data
items.text: Resources of collecting data

items.quote: Primary resources (Field resources):
items.claim: Primary resources (Field resources) are the resources from which we originally get data through interviewing or questionnaires (survey). This type is distinguished by accuracy, but it needs time and effort and is highly expensive to conduct.

items.quote: Secondary resources (historical resources):
items.claim: Secondary resources (historical resources): we can get data from authorities and agencies that formally work, such as the central agency for mobilization and statistics, internet and media. This type is a good type of resource because it saves time and money.
items.notes: Printed with numbered marker 2. Printed 'agancies' (spelling slip).

items.quote: Secondary resources (historical resources):
items.caption: Picture of a woman seated at a computer showing a bar chart on the screen; illustrates secondary resources.

items.quote: The method of collecting data
items.text: The method of collecting data

items.quote: determined according to the aim and the size of the statistical society
items.text: The method of collecting data is determined according to the aim and the size of the statistical society under study.

items.quote: For example: The students of a school
items.text: For example: The students of a school represent a statistical society whose value is the student.

items.quote: The students of a school
items.caption: Photo of a crowd of school students; illustrates a statistical society.

items.quote: First: Method of mass population:
items.text: First: Method of mass population:

items.quote: It means to collect the data related to the phenomenon
items.claim: Method of mass population means collecting the data related to the phenomenon of the statistical society. It is used to include all the society, such as the population. It includes all the values and is unbiased, and the outcomes are very accurate.

items.quote: Method of mass population
items.caption: Clip-art picture of people with a telescope/survey scene and a woman at a computer; illustrates the method of mass population.

items.quote: The disadvantages of such a method are ; it needs long time
items.text: The disadvantages of such a method are: it needs long time and great efforts. Furthermore, it costs much money.

items.quote: Second: Mehods of samples:
items.text: Second: Mehods of samples:

items.quote: It mainly depends upon selecting a sample from the statistical society
items.text: It mainly depends upon selecting a sample from the statistical society that it represents.

items.quote: We conduct reseaches on the sample. The outcomes we get
items.text: We conduct researches on the sample. The outcomes we get are generalized on the whole society.

items.quote: Advantages of using methods of samples:
items.text: Advantages of using methods of samples:

items.quote: It saves time, efforts and money.
items.claim: Advantage 1: using samples saves time, efforts and money.

items.quote: The only way to collect data about gigantic societies (like fish).
items.claim: Advantage 2: it is the only way to collect data about gigantic societies (like fish).

items.quote: The only method to study some limited societies such as:
items.claim: Advantage 3: it is the only method to study some limited societies, such as the two cases below.

items.quote: Check the patient blood by getting a sample
items.claim: A: Check the patient's blood by getting a sample (checking the whole blood leads to death).
items.notes: Photo of a blood sample being taken printed beside it; treated as illustrative.

items.quote: Check the production of a factory producing electric lamps
items.claim: B: Check the production of a factory producing electric lamps to determine the validity of the lamp (know for how long the lamp can be used before getting burned).

items.quote: the sample is called biased.
items.claim: A disadvantage of sample methods: outcomes are not accurate if the selected sample doesn't represent all the society well; in such a case the sample is called biased.

items.quote: How we select samples and the conditions must be found
items.text: How we select samples and the conditions must be found in getting a sample:

items.quote: First: the biased selction (samples are not randomly selected)
items.text: First: the biased selction (samples are not randomly selected)

items.quote: we select the sample in a way to satisfy the objectives
items.claim: Biased selection means selecting the sample in a way to satisfy the objectives of the research; this is called a deliberate sample.

items.quote: when we want to know how the students understood a lesson
items.text: For example, when we want to know how the students understood a lesson in mathematics we must analyze the outcomes of the test by considering the outcomes of a group of students studied the same topic without the other students; this is not a random selection.

items.quote: Second: Random seclecion (random samples)
items.text: Second: Random seclecion (random samples)

items.quote: the chance of getting any value from the society is equal
items.claim: Random selection means selecting a sample such that the chance of getting any value from the society is equal.

items.quote: Of the most important types of the random samples :
items.text: Of the most important types of the random samples:

items.quote: Simple random sample: Is the simplest type of samples
items.claim: 1. Simple random sample: the simplest type of sample; it can be got from homogeneous societies where selection is related to the size and number of units in the society.

items.quote: If the size of the society is small:
items.claim: A. If the size of the society is small: when choosing 5 students of a 40-student class, prepare an identical card for each student with name or number, put them in a box, draw a card randomly and return it again; repeat until the sample needed is obtained.
items.notes: Photo of drawing cards from a box printed beside it. Text says 'return the ball back again' (as printed).

items.quote: If the size of the society is big:
items.claim: If the size of the society is big (e.g. selecting a sample of 5 students from 800): number the students from 1 to 800, then use the calculator or Excel to give 10 random digits in the field from 0.000 to 0.999, remove the decimal point so the field runs from zero to 999, and discard the digits that are more than 800.
items.notes: Printed as point B under the sampling methods; the previous page's method 'If the size of the society is small:' is point A.

items.quote: start
items.caption: Calculator key sequence after 'start': ON, SHIFT, Ran# (the dot key), = keys, then a calculator display showing 'Ran #' and 0.624.
items.notes: Key labels read from small image; verify. A separate calculator photo at top right is decorative.

items.quote: Repeat pressing on the appearence of numbers will be successive.
items.text: Repeat pressing on the = key; the appearance of numbers will be successive.
items.notes: An = key image is printed inline in the sentence.

items.quote: 5 digits unrepreated are enough to give the digits
items.claim: Five non-repeated digits are enough to give the numbers of the sample of students.
items.notes: Printed with a circled number 2 marker.

items.quote: Layer random sample:
items.claim: When the society to be examined is heterogeneous or made up of qualitative sets that differ in characteristics, it is divided into homogeneous sets according to the characteristics forming it. Each set is called a layer, and the researcher selects a random sample in which each layer is represented according to its size in the society. Such a sample is called the layer sample.

items.quote: For example: when we want to study an educational level
items.text: For example: to study the educational level of a society of 400 persons where the ratio of males to females is 3:2, with a sample of 50 persons, we must select 30 persons from the male layer and 20 persons from the female layer randomly.
items.notes: Printed as 'For example', not a numbered Example. A photo of a crowd of students is decorative.

learning_objectives.label: Resources of collecting data
learning_objectives.description: Distinguish primary resources from secondary resources of collecting data and state the advantages of each.

learning_objectives.label: Methods of collecting data
learning_objectives.description: Identify the method of collecting data (method of mass population or method of samples) suited to the aim and size of the statistical society, stating its advantages and disadvantages.

learning_objectives.label: Selecting types of samples
learning_objectives.description: Select a sample using a biased choice, a simple random sample or a layer sample, and decide how many units to take from each layer.
